source.title: Scaling Vision Transformers for Functional MRI with Flat Maps
source.authors: Connor Lane; Mihir Tripathy; L. Murali; Ratna Sagari Grandhi; Shamus Sim Zi Yang; Sam Gijsen; Debojyoti Das; M. Ram; Utkarsh Singh; Cesar Kadir Torrico Villanueva; Yu-Xiang Wei; Will Beddow; Gianfranco Cortés; Suin Cho; Daniel Z. Kaplan; Benjamin Warner; Tanishq Mathew Abraham; Paul S. Scotti

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It directly studies scaling in fMRI, a new modality and training regime, using masked-reconstruction loss and downstream probes rather than language-model cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a data-size and model-size scaling analysis for fMRI reconstruction loss, plus downstream probe performance across those scales. Results cited from language-model scaling papers are not recorded as this study's results. The paper's broader representation comparisons and benchmark comparisons are not rows for the claim versions unless they report a scale-dependent outcome.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to held-out fMRI masked-autoencoder reconstruction loss across data size (0.4M–6.6M frames) and encoder size (2M–168M), and tracks downstream probes across both sweeps. Its results bear on V5 (new modality), V2 (fits on the three smallest settings tested on larger ones), V6 and V7 (curves bending away from the power law).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct for the scaling part. The authors claim the first rigorous fMRI scaling laws (strict power law in-distribution) while highlighting limits of scaling with homogeneous data: weak OOD generalization, model-size saturation at 37M, and a need for data diversity. The paper's wider conclusions also cover flat maps performing best on state decoding and no model clearly beating a functional-connectivity baseline on trait prediction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses masked-autoencoder reconstruction loss on fMRI rather than next-token held-out cross-entropy; varies fMRI data quantity and encoder size, without a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Scaling outcomes vary between in-distribution HCP-YA and out-of-distribution NSD; model-size gains saturate at depth 9 (37M encoder parameters).
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The scaling evidence is limited to fMRI masked reconstruction and a single main model family. Reconstruction loss scaling is plotted rather than numerically tabulated; the tested scaling ranges do not establish extrapolation over several orders of magnitude. Out-of-distribution results weaken and model-size improvements saturate.
record.rows_left_out: None. Cited language-model scaling results and other non-scale-dependent benchmark comparisons were not recorded as this study's scaling results.

untested.parts: Not language-model cross-entropy; the loss is fMRI MAE reconstruction MSE.
Extrapolation over several orders of magnitude; the tested ranges are about 1 order (data) and under 2 orders (params), and the fits span only ~3x.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/data split.
Depth is scaled with fixed proportions, so parameter count changes. There is no shape comparison at fixed parameters for loss.
Only fMRI MAE pretraining; no image/video, repeated-data or fine-tuning scaling laws.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions or compute-optimal splits.

missing.what: Downstream accuracy versus pretraining steps for HCP-YA and UKBB data subsets under full cosine schedules. There is no clear benefit of more data on NSD COCO24, UKBB with 10x more data underperforms HCP-YA, and the smallest UKBB subset is best on NSD. The authors note tension with Fig 7c, which uses intermediate checkpoints.
Fitted power-law exponents and constants shown in the figure: data L=(N/15)^-0.014 and (N/7)^-0.017; params L=(P/4)^-0.012 and (P/0)^-0.008. Assignment to HCP-YA vs NSD is unclear in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 'supports' on r3 is wrong: the model-size fit comes from the three smallest models and fails beyond them. Its V7 limits_scope entry described untested parts, so it was moved to untested. r10 was changed to partial. The downstream data-scaling rows rest on intermediate checkpoints, which Appendix C.2 says conflict with full-schedule results.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses fMRI masked-reconstruction loss, not held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
It fits curves using the three smallest data splits or models and evaluates larger settings, but the tested ranges do not establish prediction across multiple orders of magnitude.
No fixed-compute sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is reported.
The scaling analysis does not compare depth, width, or architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
The study tests fMRI masked-autoencoder pretraining, not image/video-model scaling, repeated-data scaling, fine-tuning, or transfer as general training regimes.
It reports downstream accuracy scaling with data and model size, but does not test a predictive relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance.
It shows weaker out-of-distribution scaling and model-size saturation, but does not compare alternative fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions, or compute-optimal splits.

rows.subject: CortexMAE flat map (ViT-B)
rows.operation_detail: Pretrained on varying HCP-YA training-data subsets; power laws estimated from the three smallest data splits.

conditions.value: training data: 400K to 6.6M frames (110 hours to 1.8K hours)

rows.value: Strict power-law decrease; reported exponent -0.01 (compared in text with -0.1 for Kaplan et al. language modeling).
rows.note: The plotted loss values are not transcribed as exact numbers in the text. The scaling analysis uses the three smallest data splits to estimate the curve.
rows.check: Fine as a V5/V2 row. Range is ~16x data (about 1.2 orders), with the fit on the three smallest splits (0.5–1.6M). Fitted exponents in Fig 7a are about -0.014 and -0.017; the footnote rounds to -0.01 vs Kaplan's -0.1, which bears on V7.

source_check.correct: V5: observed. V2: cannot_determine for the specified orders-of-magnitude extrapolation; the largest split is about 4× the largest fitted split. The reported exponent comparison bears on V7.
source_check.problem: The observed state is appropriate for V5 but overstates what the extrapolation span establishes for V2.

rows.subject: CortexMAE flat map (ViT-B)

rows.note: The authors describe slower-than-predicted improvement on NSD and raise data diversity as a possible requirement for generalization.
rows.check: State correct. NSD is out of distribution, and loss improves more slowly than the fitted power law.

source_check.correct: Partial for the power-law behavior and extrapolation in V5/V2; observed for V7's departure from a single power law.
